authored_by: Digital Oil Sticker (our own model — NOT manufacturer guidance)
basis_statement: Grades follow the SAE J300 engine-oil viscosity classification. Base-stock interval characteristics and severe-service definitions follow widely published industry guidance. Engine classes are derived by us from EPA/DOE configuration fields. Every interval here is OUR model, is labeled as such in the UI, and is overridden by any sourced manufacturer schedule (shorter always wins).
safety_rule: For any combination we do not have an explicit rule for, use the LOWEST interval of the applicable published range. Never extrapolate upward.

oil_grades.notes: Ultra-low viscosity; specific late-model hybrids only.
Late-model fuel-economy engines; only where specified.
The most widely specified grade across eras.
Light-duty diesel and European performance specs.
Older gasoline engines and warm climates.

base_stocks.reasoning: Mineral base oils oxidize and shear sooner than synthetics; published general guidance clusters at 3,000-5,000 miles with a roughly 6-month time cap.
Partial synthetic content improves oxidation resistance over conventional but does not reach full-synthetic stability.

Engineered base stocks resist thermal breakdown and oxidation longest; published guidance clusters at 7,500-10,000 miles, with some OEM specifications extending further — we do not extend beyond the published range without a sourced schedule.

High-mileage oils are an additive package (seal conditioners, anti-wear) layered on a conventional or synthetic base. The additives address leaks and wear, NOT drain interval, so we treat the interval as blend-equivalent unless the user selects a full-synthetic high-mileage product.

engine_classes.reasoning: No internal-combustion engine and therefore no engine oil service.
Fuel-cell drivetrain has no engine oil service.
Diesel oils carry soot and require diesel-rated service categories. Interval follows the base-stock range but the service category is not interchangeable with gasoline oils.

Total engine run time is lower than a comparable conventional drivetrain, but frequent cold starts and short engine-on cycles offset the benefit. We hold the base-stock interval and lean on the time cap.
Direct-injection engines are prone to fuel dilution of the oil, which lowers effective viscosity and shortens useful oil life. We shorten the interval by 20% and prefer synthetic.
Small-displacement port-injected gasoline engines hold less oil but run lower loads; the base-stock range applies.
Mainstream port-injected gasoline engines; the base-stock range applies.
Larger sumps dilute contamination, but these engines are more often used for towing and hauling. We hold the base range rather than extending it.
Fallback for engines we cannot classify (natural gas, rotary, incomplete data). Per the safety rule we shorten the interval and suggest the most common grade only as a starting point.

service_conditions.reasoning: Mostly longer trips at steady speeds in moderate conditions.

Published severe-service definitions consistently include frequent short trips (especially in cold weather), extended idling and stop-and-go traffic, towing or hauling, dusty conditions, and sustained extreme temperatures. Industry guidance roughly halves the interval.
questions: Towing, hauling, or carrying heavy loads
Sustained very hot or very cold temperatures
